- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially < 0.3) — add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag 1–3 days behind true price movements — adjust forward by 1–2 days if sentiment is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes — cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak if sentiment drops sharply.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- Sentiment > 0.6 correlates with higher volatility — increase forecast variance by 5–10% for 3–5 day horizon.
- If sentiment is flat (0.3–0.4) and price is rising, forecast may be too conservative — add 1–2% to forecast for next 3 days.
